Capabilities.Explanation: The collector requires enabled Security Defaults or at least one enabled Conditional Access policy.
The collector requires Security Defaults or an enabled privileged-role policy with MFA or authentication strength.
The collector requires Security Defaults or an all-user block for the legacy client types.
The collector counts the complete bounded Global Administrator assignment collection.
The authorization-policy invitation enum is compared with this allow-list.
The default-user application creation permission is compared with this boolean.
Default-user permission grant policy assignments are compared with the consent baseline.
The isolated Exchange adapter evaluates the configured modern-authentication requirement.
The isolated Exchange adapter evaluates SMTP client authentication.
The isolated Exchange adapter evaluates POP3.
The isolated Exchange adapter evaluates IMAP4.
The isolated Exchange adapter evaluates automatic forwarding and related mail flow evidence.
The isolated Exchange adapter evaluates Exchange DKIM evidence.
The isolated Exchange adapter evaluates organization audit evidence.
The Graph collector compares the tenant sharing capability with this ceiling.
The Graph collector evaluates the returned legacy-authentication setting.
The Graph collector evaluates the returned guest-acceptance setting.
The Graph collector evaluates the returned unmanaged-sync setting.
The Graph collector evaluates the returned blocked-extension list.
The Graph collector compares the returned retention period with this minimum.
The collector evaluates in-scope Azure role assignments against these high-risk role names.
The collector permits high-risk role assignments only for listed Azure principal object IDs.
Azure CLI reads the Microsoft Graph service principal role map and its complete bounded app-role assignments.
The collector requires enabled, in-subscription Activity Log alerts with action groups covering each configured category.
The collector evaluates storage-account network default actions.
The collector evaluates returned Key Vault purge-protection properties.
The selected region scopes the current CloudTrail query; it does not enumerate or validate all active regions.
The collector compares the IAM password minimum length with this floor.
The collector compares the IAM password maximum age with this ceiling.
The collector compares IAM password reuse prevention with this floor.
The collector compares active IAM user access-key creation times with this maximum age.
The collector requires an active, successfully delivering VPC Flow Log for every collected VPC.
The collector evaluates the root-account MFA summary flag.
The collector requires a returned CloudTrail trail to be multi-region when this policy is enabled.
The collector requires a returned CloudTrail trail to validate delivered log files when this policy is enabled.
The collector allows only declared single TCP ports on public security-group ingress.
The collector rejects public security-group ingress outside the declared allow-list when enabled.
When configured, the selected project's parent organization is compared with this identifier.
The collector evaluates primitive IAM role members against this allow-list.
The collector compares enabled user-managed service-account key creation times with this maximum age.
The collector evaluates allServices IAM audit configuration against these required log types.
The collector evaluates project common metadata for enable-oslogin.
The collector requires an enabled user-managed logging sink with an explicit destination; destination retention remains outside this control.
The tailnet name scopes an API reachability check; policy configuration is not evaluated.
The complete bounded device inventory is checked against the last-seen threshold.
Auth-key creation and expiry timestamps are compared with this maximum lifetime.
Collected auth-key device capabilities are checked for reusable keys.
Collected auth-key device capabilities are checked for preauthorized keys.
The JSON tailnet policy is checked for supported universal allow-all ACLs and grants.
This is a local authorization boundary, not an internet posture control.
Bounded candidates are checked through the configured DoH resolver and form the optional dnsx wordlist.
The DNS collector requires authenticated DNSSEC evidence when this setting is enabled.
The DNS collector checks the configured selectors.
The declared resolver name is retained as evidence provenance and does not establish DNS security.
Passive DNS uses only this explicit HTTPS resolver endpoint; it never falls back to a public resolver.
This operator declaration identifies a resolver intended for private-zone collection; it is retained as provenance, not independently verified.
The bounded resolver timeout limits collection but does not evaluate a cloud security control.
Up to two explicitly configured secondary DoH resolvers are compared against desired RRsets and the primary resolver.
Observed TTLs for desired RRsets must not fall below this bound.
Observed TTLs for desired RRsets must not exceed this bound.
Provider-neutral BIND exports use this TTL, which must remain within the policy bounds.
The DNS collector compares each declared RRset with observed public DNS evidence.
When enabled, Claudit invokes dnsx only for the bounded configured wordlist.
The validated executable name is used without shell evaluation.
The optional dnsx run uses this request-per-second ceiling.
Optional dnsx discovery uses only this explicitly configured resolver list when non-empty.
dnsx receives this query timeout and remains subject to Claudit's global CLI deadline.
Wildcard TCP listeners are compared with SSH and this explicit public-port allow-list.
A package-manager simulation count is compared with this maximum.
The collector checks UFW, firewalld or nftables for an active ruleset.
The collector checks for a readable auth log or SSH system journal evidence.
The effective sshd configuration must report passwordauthentication no.
The effective sshd configuration must report permitrootlogin no.
Each provider inventory retains at most the configured asset count plus one overflow sentinel; larger estates are reported as intentionally partial.
